description.value: This study investigated whether real-time fMRI neurofeedback can train emotion regulation by down-regulating amygdala activity and alter task-specific amygdala connectivity across four training sessions.

spans.text: The clinical potential of rt-fMRI neurofeedback as a treatment tool for psychotherapy of disorders of emotion regulation requires sustained amygdala down-regulation over multiple sessions

value: We hypothesized that four weekly feedback-supported cognitive emotion regulation training sessions would improve down-regulation of amygdala activity over sessions, and this effect is stronger than training without feedback.

We hypothesized that the beta weights in the regulate condition would decrease from the first to the fourth session as compared to the view condition and that this effect would be more pronounced in the Feedback group than in the Control group.

description.value: The study used a single-blind design with feedback and control groups, and four weekly training sessions.
